mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 4%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive equity returns, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time when UNRATE is below 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it indicates a potential overheating economy, leading to inflation concerns and negative equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time when GDPC1 growth is strong and FEDFUNDS is high, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals continued economic growth, leading to positive equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time when INDPRO increases during late-cycle, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative more than 35% of the time when PAYEMS grows, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates strong demand, which is positive for equities, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 45% of the time when RSAFS increases by over 5%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low, it indicates a tight labor market and potential inflation, leading to negative equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive more than 25% of the time when FEDFUNDS is high and UNRATE is low, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during a housing market recovery indicates economic expansion, leading to positive equity returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time when HOUST increases during recovery, the hypothesis is falsified.
